title: DataAccessV1dot21
description: K-05 v1.21, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1508: a commit may raise one live open question's ask count by one, so K-09 v1.12's re-sent question has its cap; K-09 v1.12 open gap 173; DL-1018, DL-1030, DL-1033). It only adds to v1.20 (data-access.v1.20.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to every earlier version down to v1): every v1.20 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes but the five it restates, each taking only a new optional list or a new refusal, so every v1 to v1.20 exchange is a v1.21 exchange. Restated: writes (openQuestions may hold askAgain, at most one raise, never beside a close), commitTurn.request (to refer to v1.21's writes), commitTurn.errors (wrongState may name an open question that is not live), commitTurn.exchange (to refer to both, v1.17's handle-id rule kept by reference) and commitTurn.handleIdExchange (to narrow v1.21's exchange). Added: openQuestionAskAgain (a raise: the question's id and the version the turn read; README item 81), openQuestionWrongStateError, and commitTurn.askAgainExchange (commitTurn.exchange narrowed to a request that raises, the definition the v1.21 fixtures are listed under). A raise moves the question's ask_count and version by one and nothing else, and its event-log entry is the request's own open_question.asked_again, a K-08 v1 kind (README default 196). No call, column, grant, index or migration is added: ask_count is K-04 v1's (migration 0009). writePlan, markPart and readFixedLineFacts keep their shapes: what README defaults 200 to 205 add to them (the opener mark, its read fallback, the opt-out line's delivery time) is in the README alone. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

openQuestionAskAgain.title: OpenQuestionAskAgain
openQuestionAskAgain.description: An open question the turn asks again (README item 81; K-09 v1.12 defaults 192 and 194 and its open gap 173): its ask count raised by one (K-04 v1 open_questions.ask_count; arch 09 line 490: 'Rosie asks once; once more only after a language or access problem, or after answering a question back') and its version raised by one, compared and set at the version the turn read, with the turn's other writes, all or nothing. Refused versionChanged when its version moved since (limit 4: arch 06 line 305), as any update is, and wrongState when it is not live, waiting or open, at that version (openQuestionWrongStateError). It names the version, never the count: the count written is the stored count plus one, which the compare makes the count the turn read plus one (README default 192). Nothing else of the question moves: its status, options, read-back, versions read, Clock line, bundle, turn and clock row stay as they are; its send time and poll are read from the rows that ask it (README v1.2 default 41; migration 0037), so they become the re-sent row's once a part of that row has gone, never at the commit (README default 195). New in v1.21.

expectVersion.description: The version the turn read the question at; the raise sets it one higher or the commit is refused (limit 4).

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: Everything one turn commits, all or nothing, in one transaction under the turn id (arch 01 lines 39 to 41; arch 02 line 121; 02-contracts K-05 item 1): v1.1's writes with one more list. From v1.21 (T-1508; README item 81) openQuestions may hold askAgain, the one open question the turn asks again, its ask count raised by one, left out when the turn raises none, so every v1 to v1.20 commit is a v1.21 commit. Restated in v1.21 only to take it: every other list is v1.1's own, by reference to v1.1's definition of it, which v1.2 to v1.20 keep unchanged. A commit that asks a question again closes none (openQuestions.close empty when askAgain is given), so a question is never raised and closed together (README default 194; refuse-commit-s1-02-asks-again-and-closes). A firing's writes (fireClock.request) stay v1.1's: only a turn's commit asks a question again (README default 199). Changed in v1.21.

openQuestions.description: The open questions the turn opens (open, v1's), closes (close, v1's) and, from v1.21, asks again (askAgain). With askAgain, close is empty (README default 194).

askAgain.description: The open question the turn asks again, at most one a commit (README item 81; default 194): its id and the version the turn read (openQuestionAskAgain). Left out when the turn raises none, never empty, so a commit that raises nothing has one spelling; a second raise, of the same question or another, is refused (refuse-commit-s1-02-asks-again-twice). Its one writer today is K-09 v1.12's asked part, which sends the turn's one open question again (K-09 v1.12 defaults 192 to 194; T-1505). New in v1.21.

commitTurn.request.title: CommitTurnRequest
commitTurn.request.description: Commit a turn: the gate has passed limits 1 to 6, and one transaction writes the turn row (committed), the state, open questions, clock rows, outbox rows, reservations and the event log under the turn id, all or nothing, once (arch 01 lines 39 to 41; arch 02 line 121; arch 10 line 508; 02-contracts K-05 item 1). v1.1 (T-071): its writes may also hold effects and waitingChat. v1.17 (T-1418; README item 71) adds answerPhoneRowsBy, which changes only what the call answers. v1.21 (T-1508; README item 81): its writes may hold openQuestions.askAgain, one open question asked again. Restated in v1.21 only to refer to v1.21's writes: turn and versionsRead are v1.1's own and answerPhoneRowsBy v1.17's, each by reference, so without askAgain the request is v1.20's. Changed in v1.21.

openQuestionWrongStateError.title: OpenQuestionWrongStateError
openQuestionWrongStateError.description: An open question a commit asks again that is not live: at the version the turn read, its status is answered, defaulted or withdrawn (README item 81, default 193). v1.1's wrongState for one more table: the same error and fields, its table open_questions and its state the question's status now (K-04 v1 open_questions.status; arch 09 line 490), never waiting or open. Nothing was written. A question closed after the turn read it has a newer version and is answered versionChanged first (limit 4), so wrongState answers a raise of a question the turn read already closed. New in v1.21.

state.description: Its status now (K-04 v1 open_questions.status), a closed one.

commitTurn.errors.title: CommitTurnErrors
commitTurn.errors.description: Refused, nothing written: v1.1's errors, by reference (the rows that changed, limit 4; the reservation no longer held, limit 5; the turn already parked; a database rule; a transient failure; wrongState for an effect let go that is not in outage), and from v1.21 (T-1508; README item 81) wrongState for an open question asked again that is not live (openQuestionWrongStateError). Changed in v1.21.

commitTurn.exchange.title: CommitTurnExchange
commitTurn.exchange.description: One commitTurn request with its outcome, restated in v1.21 to refer to v1.21's commitTurn.request and commitTurn.errors. call and given are v1.1's own and the response v1.20's, by reference, and the answer to a request that asks for phones rows by handle id keeps v1.17's rule (README item 71): its if and then are v1.17's own, by reference. So without askAgain the exchange is v1.20's. Changed in v1.21.

commitTurn.handleIdExchange.title: CommitTurnHandleIdExchange
commitTurn.handleIdExchange.description: v1.17's narrowing to a request that carries answerPhoneRowsBy (README item 71), restated in v1.21 to narrow v1.21's commitTurn.exchange, so a commit that asks for handle ids and asks a question again is one of it; its second part is v1.17's own, by reference. Every v1.17 fixture is one of it. Changed in v1.21.

commitTurn.askAgainExchange.title: CommitTurnAskAgainExchange
commitTurn.askAgainExchange.description: The exchange of a commit that asks an open question again: commitTurn.exchange narrowed by allOf to a request whose writes hold openQuestions.askAgain (README item 81), as commitTurn.handleIdExchange narrows it to a request that asks for handle ids. The v1.21 fixtures are listed under this definition, so the loops that select commitTurn.exchange or commitTurn.handleIdExchange (db/repo/commit-turn.int.test.ts COMMIT_ENTRIES and HANDLE_ID_ENTRIES) never meet them before db/repo builds the raise (T-1509); it is the definition db/repo's answers to a request that raises are checked against (T-1509) and a caller that raises checks its exchanges by (T-1505). New in v1.21.
